prompt: My level 92 Righteous Fire Juggernaut dies on maps with reduced maximum resistances. My fire resistance is capped at 76% (90% before the cap) and life is 6,800. What's wrong?

must: Names the cause: Righteous Fire burns the character for a share of its maximum life every second as fire damage, and the build survives only while life regeneration and recovery exceed that burn after fire resistance
Says a map's reduced maximum resistances lowers the cap, so actual fire resistance drops (76% to about 64% with -12%) and the overcap does not help
Shows the size of the change: damage taken from the burn goes from 24% to about 36% of its base, roughly 50% more, so net recovery turns negative; fire hits grow by the same factor
Says this map modifier is one a Righteous Fire build normally avoids or rerolls, along with modifiers that stop or cut life regeneration and recovery
Gives the lasting fix: more maximum fire resistance and more life regeneration or recovery so the build has a margin
Asks for, or reads from the build, the life regeneration per second and the sources of maximum fire resistance before giving numbers
must_not: Says more overcapped fire resistance protects against a reduced maximum
Blames low life alone and ignores the self-burn
Says the damage taken rises by only 12%
Invents the character's regeneration or other stats that were not given

prompt: Cyclone Slayer, 5,000 life, 5 million tooltip DPS, but I die to degen ground effects and can never stand in them.

must: Names the gap: the build's recovery is leech, which only comes from hitting enemies and is capped per second; it has no recovery floor of its own against damage over time
Says tooltip DPS does not help here: damaging ground deals damage over time, which armour, block and evasion do not reduce, and leech must out-recover it
Says 5,000 life is a small buffer for an endgame melee character

Gives fixes aimed at the gap: real life regeneration, less damage over time taken or immunity to the specific ground effect (burning ground, for example), the matching resistance (chaos resistance for chaos ground), and more life
Says leaving the ground is still the right play for the worst effects
Asks for, or reads from the build, the resistances (chaos included), life regeneration and which ground effects kill the character
must_not: Recommends more damage as the fix
Says armour or block reduces damage from ground effects
Invents stats that were not given

intent: Flaw class: sustain or recovery gap.

prompt: My Ice Nova Hierophant does far less damage on bosses than the tooltip says, and enemies barely get chilled or frozen. Tooltip 3M.

must: Says a tooltip or planner figure includes conditions that may not hold on a boss: charges, temporary buffs, stand-still effects, an assumed shock or other enemy debuff, and every overlap or projectile hitting
Says to check which of those conditions are switched on and whether they are real against a boss, using the build's calculation breakdown
Says bosses have higher resistances than normal monsters, so missing penetration, exposure or a curse cuts the real damage
Explains the weak chill and freeze: they depend on the hit's cold damage compared with the boss's ailment threshold, which is very high; a chill under the 5% minimum is not applied
Says only the cold part of the hit counts, so a build whose damage is mostly another type (lightning from Archmage, for example) chills and freezes poorly
Gives fixes for the ailments: more cold damage per hit, converting damage to cold, an effect that lets the other damage type freeze, or a source of fixed-value chill
Asks which conversion, curse, exposure and shock sources the build uses, or reads them from the build
must_not: Says bosses are immune to chill or freeze as a general rule
Uses the hit's total damage for chill and freeze
Says bosses have less curse effect on them (removed in 3.20)
States the build's gems or items as fact when they were not given

intent: Flaw class: tooltip conditions or scaling that do not hold against bosses.

prompt: Toxic Rain Pathfinder: I swapped my bow for one with higher physical DPS and my damage went down. Why?

must: Says Toxic Rain's damage is mostly the chaos damage over time from its spore pods, and that damage over time has a base set by the gem's level, not by the weapon's damage
Says a bow's physical DPS only raises the small hit, so a higher physical DPS bow gives almost nothing
Says what does scale it: gem level, chaos and generic damage over time multiplier, damage over time and chaos damage, attack speed (more pods) and skill duration
Concludes the new bow lost stats that mattered: attack speed, added gem levels or damage over time multiplier
Notes the exception: a poison version of the build does use hit damage
Asks for, or compares, the stats of the old and new bow
must_not: Says weapon physical damage scales the pod damage over time
Recommends a higher physical DPS bow as the upgrade
Treats the tooltip's hit damage as the build's damage

intent: Flaw class: stat-scaling mismatch between item and build.
